summary: In this story, a neighborhood turns a trash-filled empty lot into a shared vegetable garden, and a shy girl discovers new friends and a love of growing things.
introduce: Show the title “The Garden That Grew Hope” and ask, “What do you think will happen in this story, and why?” Explain that good readers use clues in the text together with what they already know to make inferences.

keyTerms.def: a group of people who live in the same area
the top layer of earth where plants grow
a person who offers to help without being paid

challengeTerms.def: to work jointly with others on a shared task
to prepare land and grow plants on it
to change something completely, often for the better

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that working together on a shared project is more rewarding than working alone? Use evidence from the story to explain.
Explain how both the neighborhood and Lina changed by the end of the story.
struggling: Read the first part of the story aloud together, review community, soil, and volunteer, and let weak readers answer “What clue tells you that?” questions using sentence starters.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses collaborate, cultivate, and transform to make an inference that the story does not state and support it with two clues.
